text_blocks.snippet: In vivo therapy refers to treatments where a therapeutic substance or procedure is administered directly into the body of a living organism, typically a patient. This contrasts with ex vivo therapy, where cells are modified outside the body and then introduced. In the context of gene therapy, in vivo means delivering the therapeutic gene directly to the target cells within the body, often using a viral vector.
